page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top, with the page number at top left. Centred heading "CONCIO VIII." with the scripture reference "Genef. 21." below it. Then one block of italic text, set in one paragraph with a woodcut initial. Catchword at the lower right.

p.i: VISITAVIT autem Dominus Saram, quemadmodum dixerat: fecitq; dominus Sara, sicut loquutus fuerat. Nam concepit & peperit Sara ipsi Abraham filium in senectute sua, idq; illo tempore, quod prædixerat ei Deus. Et Abraham vocauit nomen filii sui, qui sibi natus erat, & quem sibi genuerat Sara, Isahac. Circumcidit quoque Abraham Isahac filium suum, cum esset filius octo dierum, quemadmodum præceperat illi Deus. Porrò Abraham fuit filius centum annorum, cum sibi nasceretur Isahac filius suus. Sara verò dixit: risum fecit mihi Deus, ut omnis qui audierit, corrideat mihi. Dixitq;, quis unquam dixit Abraha, lactauit Sara filios? siquidem genvi filium in senectute illius. Creuit itaque puer & ablactatus est, fecitq; Abraham convivium magnum illo die cum ablactaretur Isahac. Et vidit Sara filium Hagar Ae-gyptia, quem illa genuit ipsi Abraham, esse derisorem. Unde dixit ad Abraham: eijce[?]

page.notes: The woodcut initial V is joined to "ISITAVIT", so it reads "VISITAVIT". "Abraham" is printed with a small sign before the name, which I have not reproduced. "eijce" at the foot is the catchword. Its last letters are hard to read, so I marked them with [?]. Changes from the printed spelling: "Creuit" is written "Creuit" as printed, "genuerat" and "genui" are printed with u, "conuiuium" is printed with uiu, and u/v and i/j are normalised where a consonant or vowel was clear. Where the printed form was uncertain, I kept the printed letters.
